Angles written ∠ are read from the figure. ∡(a, b) is the angle through which line a must be turned counter-clockwise to become parallel to b, taken modulo 180°; ∡XYZ means ∡(YX, YZ). These angles do not depend on how the figure is drawn. Directed angles are needed only in step 7, where the figure-angle form would depend on the configuration. Let M be the midpoint of BC. Let N be the midpoint of AC.

Plan: it suffices to show that AH ∥ OM and △AHG ∼ △MOG.

1. G is the centroid of △ABC, so AG : GM = 2. (1)

2. OA = OC and NA = NC, so ON is the perpendicular bisector of AC; hence ON ⟂ AC. (2)

3. OB = OC and MB = MC, so OM is the perpendicular bisector of BC; hence OM ⟂ BC. (3)

4. AH ⟂ BC and OM ⟂ BC, by (3), so AH ∥ OM. (4)

5. We show that △AHB ∼ △MON:

∠HAB = ∠B − 90°    [AH ⟂ BC]
     = 90° − ∠BMN    [MN is a midline of △CBA]
     = ∠OMN    [OM ⟂ BC, by (3)]

∠ABH = ∠A + 90°    [BH ⟂ AC]
     = ∠MNC + 90°    [MN is a midline of △CBA]
     = ∠MNO    [ON ⟂ AC, by (2)]

Hence △AHB ∼ △MON. (5)

6. AH ∥ OM, by (4), so ∠HAG = ∠OMA.

MG / AG = 1 / 2    [AG : GM = 2, by (1)]
        = MN / AB    [MN is a midline of △CBA]
        = OM / AH    [△AHB ∼ △MON, by (5)]

Hence △AHG ∼ △MOG. (6)

7. We show that O, G, H are collinear:

∡OGH = ∡(OM, AH)    [△AHG ∼ △MOG, by (6)]
     = 0°    [AH ∥ OM, by (4)]

So O, G, H are collinear, as required. ∎
